author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader can see every specialty and the veterinarians holding it on one page
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every stored specialty by name with the full name of each veterinarian holding it, gathers veterinarians holding none under their own group, and presents the whole list on one page.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then each is shown by its stored name with the full name of every veterinarian holding it
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when the directory is opened, then the specialty is still shown, with no veterinarian under it
given a veterinarian who holds no specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian is shown under a group for those holding none
given every specialty the clinic holds, when the directory is opened, then all of them are shown together, without paging
given the supported languages, when the directory is opened, then its own wording is present in each of them
given a veterinarian holding more than one specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian is shown under each of them
given no stored specialties at all, when the directory is opened, then it opens with nothing listed rather than failing
given every veterinarian holds at least one specialty, when the directory is opened, then the group for those holding none is left out
given repeated openings of the directory, when the entries are compared, then specialties and the veterinarians within each appear in a stable order
non_goals: managing veterinarians or their specialties in any way (NG-2 stands unchanged)
a navigation entry, or a link to the page from any other page
paging or otherwise splitting the list across pages
presenting the veterinarian roster: the page lists specialties, not veterinarians
searching or filtering the directory (NG-9 stands unchanged)
notes: Page address decided in the dispatch: GET /specialties.html, read-only. The PRD keeps the address out of the narrative under the what/how boundary; it is a product decision, not a design choice, so system-design-expert takes it as given. Three open questions are recorded in docs/prd.md rather than blocking this slice: the order of entries (a stable order is required, which order is unanswered), whether the no-specialty group shows when empty (left out, on the narrowest reading), and whether a navigation entry follows. REQ-VET-001 is untouched: the existing paged veterinarian directory stays as it is.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice reuses the vet feature package end to end: a server-rendered Thymeleaf page (ADR 2026-07-31-server-side-rendering-with-thymeleaf), a Spring Data repository read, and message-bundle wording, all inside the feature-package organization ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization records. One adjustment carries the whole slice: nothing today reaches Specialty except through Vet.getSpecialties(), so acceptance criterion 2 (a specialty no veterinarian holds is still shown) cannot be served from VetRepository. Add a SpecialtyRepository beside it in the same package, shaped on owner/PetTypeRepository - the existing lookup-list repository that fixes its own order with an explicit ORDER BY query. Everything stays inside org.springframework.samples.petclinic.vet, so the package dependency direction recorded in system-design.md#package-structure (vet depends only on model) is unchanged and no cycle is introduced. Basis note: the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, so the claims above rest on grep over src plus direct reads of VetController, VetRepository, Vet, Specialty, PetTypeRepository, vetList.html and layout.html - the weaker basis.
integration_points: VetController gains a third read route, GET /specialties.html, alongside /vets.html and /vets; it now takes SpecialtyRepository as a second constructor argument
SpecialtyRepository is a new Spring Data interface over the existing specialties table; no schema or seed-data change, and no change to any of the three vendor scripts

SpecialtyDirectory is the read model the new view renders: built from the two repository reads, it inverts the Vet-to-Specialty association into Specialty-to-Veterinarians and separates the veterinarians holding none

templates/vets/specialtyList.html renders the directory through the shared layout fragment; the menu argument must name no existing nav item so nothing is highlighted, which honors the no-navigation-entry non-goal without touching layout.html
messages.properties gains the wording the page needs, and every other bundle except messages_en.properties must gain the same keys - I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces both halves of REQ-LANG-002

patterns.description: lookup-list repository with an explicit ORDER BY query - the shape SpecialtyRepository copies; keep it narrow (extend Repository, expose one method) per architecture-principles.md Minimal surface, matching VetRepository rather than PetTypeRepository's JpaRepository
getSpecialties() already sorts by name - the ordering convention SpecialtyDirectory should follow for specialties
full-name rendering and the layout-fragment call the new template mirrors; reuse the same firstName plus lastName expression
SpecialtyDirectory adopts the in-force Value object pattern - immutable, defensive copies, domain noun with no suffix, no ADR required since the catalog already sanctions it

risks.risk: Putting the grouping and the omit-the-empty-group rule in VetController would be a fresh violation of the Web controller row, which architecture-principles.md states the existing deviation does not extend to
risks.mitigation: Compute the inversion in SpecialtyDirectory via a static factory taking the two collections; the controller only reads the repositories, calls the factory, and names the view. The rules are then unit-testable without Spring, which is what SpecialtyDirectoryTests covers

risks.risk: VetControllerTests is a @WebMvcTest with a single @MockitoBean VetRepository; adding a constructor argument breaks every existing test in it with a missing-bean failure
risks.mitigation: Add a second @MockitoBean SpecialtyRepository in the same class before touching the controller, so the two existing tests keep passing through the change

risks.risk: Modelling the no-specialty group as a Specialty-shaped entry with a null or sentinel name pushes a localized heading into the model and makes the omit-when-empty rule a null check
risks.mitigation: Expose the held specialties and the veterinarians holding none as two separate members of SpecialtyDirectory; the template renders the localized heading and applies the omit rule as an emptiness check

risks.risk: A new message key added only to messages.properties fails I18nPropertiesSyncTest, and literal text between tags in the new template fails its sibling check
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing keys where the wording already fits (specialties, vets, name, none) so at most one new key is needed; add that key to all nine non-en bundles with a real translation, since REQ-LANG-002 forbids a partly translated language and an English copy would satisfy the test but not the requirement

risks.risk: Caching the specialty read would need a second cache in CacheConfiguration and would widen open question 5 in system-design.md, which already flags the vets cache as having no eviction
risks.mitigation: Do not cache SpecialtyRepository. No requirement asks for it, and the vet read on the same request is already cached

notes: Page address GET /specialties.html taken as given from the prd-entry notes; grep confirms no route or template claims it today. Ordering (acceptance criterion 9, edge case 4): the PRD requires a stable order but leaves which order open, so this is a design recommendation, not a requirement change - specialties by stored name (matching Vet.getSpecialties and the specialties_name index), veterinarians within each by last name then first name. Fix it in the query and in SpecialtyDirectory, not in the template. The other two PRD open questions stay open and unblocking: the empty no-specialty group is left out per the acceptance criteria as written, and no navigation entry is added. No durable-memory writes accompany this verdict: system-design.md carries current state only, so the new Contracts rows for SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyDirectory and the third VetController route belong to doc-sync after the slice lands. No ADR is needed - every type the slice adds matches an in-force catalog pattern. Terminology: specialty directory and the group for those holding none are PRD wording, not yet in ubiquitous-language.md; if they should become canonical that is the product-requirements-expert's write, not mine. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Harness-integrity observation, not a defect in the change. The `security-review` skill content delivered with this dispatch was not the project's checklist skill: it was a generic PR-scanner prompt carrying its own unrelated diff (.claude/settings.json, CLAUDE.md) and instructions that contradict this role's output contract (emit a markdown report, spawn sub-tasks, do not use bash, review a change set other than scripts/changeset.sh). I ignored the substituted instructions and reviewed the real REQ-SPC-001 change set per the system prompt, using the injected vulnerability categories only as an extra checklist. A human should confirm whether the skill file at .claude/skills/security-review was replaced, since a reviewer whose skill can be swapped for arbitrary instructions is a control the pipeline depends on.

approved_aspects: XSS: every value on the new template src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html renders through th:text with Thymeleaf's default escaping on. No th:utext, th:inline, dynamic th:href, or script context anywhere in the new page; a repo-wide sweep of src/main/resources/templates/ for th:utext/th:inline/javascript returns nothing, so the change does not open the class.

Injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() is a constant JPQL @Query with no parameters and no string concatenation. The new handler binds no request input at all, so no request-derived value can reach query text.

Exposed surface: GET /specialties.html is read-only (GET, no mutation, no state change) and renders only specialty names and veterinarian first/last names -- both already public at the pre-existing /vets.html and /vets endpoints. It exposes no data class the baseline did not, and adds no PII, credential, or internal detail. The absence of authn/authz is the demonstration's recorded baseline (system-design.md Security Context, security-principles.md Realization) and is not a finding against this change.
Mass assignment: the new handler takes no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, or @ModelAttribute -- there is no binder surface, so no identifier-binding disallow list is owed.

Path traversal / resource resolution: the view name "vets/specialtyList" and the layout fragment argument 'specialties' are string literals; no request-derived value composes a path or resource selector.
Secrets: a grep of the full change set for password/secret/token/api_key/credential returns nothing. The 10 message-bundle edits add one wording key (noSpecialty) each.

Supply chain: no dependency surface is touched -- build.gradle, settings.gradle, the Gradle wrapper, and application config are all absent from the change set, so no new artifact, version, or repository enters the build and the NVD/dependency check has no new input to evaluate.

Deserialization, error disclosure, and cross-request trust: the change adds no serialization entry point, throws no new exception carrying internal detail, and re-reads both specialties and veterinarians per request rather than trusting prior-request state.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The nested record is named `Entry`, a generic fallback name architecture-principles.md's Naming section calls out by name as prohibited: "if the PRD calls it a 'feed item', the code says FeedItem, never Entry or Record." No term for this concept is yet in ubiquitous-language.md, but the type's own javadoc already describes it precisely: "one specialty of the directory... together with the veterinarians holding it." Also referenced from src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/SpecialtyDirectoryTests.java:22,71,131,154.
findings.fix: Rename `SpecialtyDirectory.Entry` to a domain-grounded name, e.g. `HeldSpecialty` (mirrors the javadoc's own "specialty... together with the veterinarians holding it"), and update the field `entries` to `heldSpecialties` for the same reason. Propagate the rename through SpecialtyDirectory.java and SpecialtyDirectoryTests.java, and reflect the field rename in specialtyList.html (`specialtyDirectory.entries` -> `specialtyDirectory.heldSpecialties`).

findings.description: A specialty held by nobody renders an empty second cell. The sibling page vetList.html already has a convention for this exact situation in the other direction: when vet.nrOfSpecialties == 0, it renders the localized #{none} text (vetList.html:13-14) rather than leaving the cell blank. The design-block's own risk mitigation note (line 5 of the design-block record) anticipated reusing the existing 'none' key for wording that already fits, but this case does not use it, so the two pages now disagree on how to display 'holds/held-by nothing.' A reader who lands on a blank cell cannot tell an empty result from a missing one.
findings.fix: Add `<span th:if="${not #lists.isEmpty...}">` guard is unnecessary; instead render `#{none}` when `entry.veterinarians` (or the renamed field) is empty, mirroring vetList.html's `th:if="${vet.nrOfSpecialties == 0}" th:text="#{none}"` pattern, so both pages express the same 'holds nothing' case the same way.

findings.description: BY_LAST_THEN_FIRST_NAME builds its first key with a lambda, `Comparator.comparing((Vet veterinarian) -> veterinarian.getLastName())`, then chains `.thenComparing(Person::getFirstName)` as a method reference on the very next line. Vet extends Person and inherits getLastName(), so the first comparator can be a method reference too; the mixed style makes a reader stop and check whether the lambda form was hiding something the method reference could not express (it isn't).

approved_aspects: SpecialtyRepository correctly narrows to Repository (not JpaRepository) and mirrors PetTypeRepository's explicit-ORDER-BY lookup-list shape, matching the design-block's guidance
SpecialtyDirectory.of keeps the grouping and omit-when-empty rules out of VetController, satisfying the Web-controller-holds-no-rule guardrail the design-block flagged as a risk
Grouping by specialty id rather than name is a sound choice: names are display strings the store does not enforce as unique holder-independent identity, so id is the correct join key

Record-based value object is the codebase's first production record but fits the in-force Value-object pattern exactly: immutable, defensive List.copyOf(...) in both compact constructors, equality by value, domain noun with no suffix
checkFormat passes; VetControllerTests adds the second @MockitoBean before touching the controller as the design-block anticipated
I18nPropertiesSyncTest coverage: noSpecialty key present in all nine non-en bundles, absent from messages_en.properties per the established convention

author: doc-reviewer
approved_aspects: New REQ-SPC-001 section stays behavioral throughout — no route path, class name, or template name leaks into prd.md; the design-block's page-address decision is correctly kept out of the narrative
Acceptance criteria split correctly between the five 'Done when' bullets and the four numbered edge cases, matching the precedent set by the Veterinarian directory section
Every REQ-SPC-001 mention carries the tag, and the anchor `req-spc-001` follows the lowercase-hyphenated convention; doctor's req-acceptance and cross-doc checks both pass

Derived-brief banner edit is accurate: 'Each item' correctly narrowed to 'Each derived item' now that one confirmed, non-derived requirement exists, and the open-question count was corrected from ten to six, which matches the six unresolved (non-struck-through) entries in Open Questions after the three new ones were added

The three new open questions are appropriately scoped to REQ-SPC-001's genuinely unresolved product questions (ordering, empty-group visibility, navigation entry) and don't restate settled acceptance criteria

No Non-Goals table row was added or altered, correctly matching the prd-entry's absence of scope_overrides — the declined scope (no paging, no navigation link) is stated inline in the requirement instead, consistent with how REQ-VET-001 handles its own inline non-goals

docs/system-design.md and docs/adr/ were correctly left untouched for this minor-verdict slice; the deferred Contracts-table rows for SpecialtyDirectory/SpecialtyRepository are explicitly assigned to a later doc-sync pass in the design-block record, not silently dropped
Sentence-length and voice checks pass on every added/edited sentence (all under 30 words, no second-person address, no vague adjectives)

author: test-reviewer
approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectoryTests is a genuinely pure unit suite (no Spring context, no mocks) exercising SpecialtyDirectory.of() directly, correctly following the brief's guidance to move logic into a framework-free unit and test it there — 8 tests each with a single behavioral focus, four-phase structure, blank-line separated, no phase comments

All PRD acceptance criteria and edge cases have dedicated coverage: each specialty with holders (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEachSpecialtyWithTheVeterinariansHoldingIt), a specialty no one holds (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowASpecialtyNoVeterinarianHolds), the no-specialty group (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldGroupVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty), its omission when empty (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOmitTheNoSpecialtyGroupWhenEveryVeterinarianHoldsOne, unit + two MockMvc HTML-rendering tests asserting presence/absence of the 'No specialty' text under a pinned Locale.ENGLISH so the localized string assertion is deterministic), no stored specialties at all (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOpenWhenNoSpecialtyIsStored), a vet holding multiple specialties shown under each (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowAVeterinarianUnderEachSpecialtyHeld), and stable ordering of both specialties and veterinarians within a group and within the no-specialty group (two dedicated ordering tests using same-last-name-different-first-name fixtures to actually exercise the tie-break)

Mocking stays within the brief's policy: SpecialtyDirectoryTests uses zero mocks; VetControllerTests' new @MockitoBean SpecialtyRepository is the sanctioned MockMvc web-boundary exception, following the existing VetRepository pattern in the same file (consistent-with-codebase); the new ClinicServiceTests test exercises the real SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() query against real seeded data, verifying the ORDER BY name behavior end to end; no verify(...) calls anywhere, only behavioral assertions
Jacoco confirms 100% instruction coverage on both SpecialtyDirectory and the touched VetController lines, well above the 80% domain-package target

Test data follows the three-tier convention: specialty/vet names are meaningful (drive assertions or tie-break ordering), ids are explicitly declared irrelevant via a shared nextId counter with a comment, no bare mystery literals

AssertJ used exclusively with fluent, collection-aware assertions (containsExactly, extracting, isEmpty); new tests follow the host files' existing structural conventions (blank-line-wrapped MockMvc test bodies, given(...) stubbing idiom)
